title: Literature provenance of the RH-equivalence collection
scope: All 51 primary catalogue formulations, plus twelve separately indexed local summaries and the master-chain auxiliaries.

policy.Identified by Literature: Direct published criteria, explicitly explained standard reformulations of classical criteria, and separately marked literature-inspired opaque models. This does not claim that every project formula or name occurs verbatim in a paper.
policy.Potentially novel: The exact project formulation or construction has unresolved literature priority in a focused search. Classical ingredients, elementary variants and conditional interfaces are identified explicitly. This is not a claim of substantive novelty or correctness.
policy.independence: Neither category certifies Lean compilation, an axiom audit, RH, a new proof mechanism, or a finite accepted RH witness.
policy.method: Compare exact source criteria and hypotheses with primary papers. Bibliographic matches, coordinate/analytic reductions, and project-specific candidates are distinguished. Absence of an exact match in this limited review does not establish priority.

entries.basis: The completed-xi zero formulation of classical RH, with modern notation.
entries.title: Completed xi zeros lie on the critical line

entries.basis: Riemann uses s=1/2+it and the real-zero formulation of the centered xi function.

entries.basis: Squaring s−1/2 maps critical-line zeros to the nonpositive real axis; evenness makes the square descent well-defined.

entries.relationship: Bespoke angular specialization of classical entire-product positivity
entries.basis: The closed-interval within-derivative of |theta(r(x+i sqrt(1-x²)))|² was not located as an exact published RH criterion. Standard negative-real-zero product arguments are classical. Sondow–Dumitrescu concern horizontal lines in the xi plane, not these circles.
entries.title: Nonnegative within-derivative on the closed angular interval

entries.basis: No exact angular-semicircle criterion located. Passing from a smooth profile’s monotonicity to a nonnegative interior derivative is elementary analysis; this is not evidence of a separate new mechanism.
entries.title: Nonnegative ordinary angular slope on every open semicircle

entries.relationship: Logarithmic-derivative restatement of angular profile positivity
entries.basis: No exact regular-locus condition Im(z theta′/theta)≥0 was located. The chain-rule relation to E13 and logarithmic-derivative pole arguments are classical. The cited horizontal xi criteria do not state this angular Euler derivative.
entries.title: Nonnegative Euler logarithmic slope on the regular locus

entries.relationship: Endpoint minimum strengthening from real-negative-zero products
entries.basis: No exact derivative-minimum-at-x=-1 plus endpoint sign criterion located. Convexity/positivity of products of affine positive factors is standard; the particular theta profile and endpoint packaging are the unlocated formulation.
entries.title: Left endpoint minimizes the angular derivative and has nonnegative derivative

entries.basis: For fixed r and positive normalizer, exp(L) D_x L=(epsilon/S(r)²) D_x P. Thus the flux condition repackages E15. No exact publication located; this row should not imply independent substantive novelty of logarithmic flux.

entries.title: Logarithmic flux master with the actual theta normalizer

entries.basis: No exact criterion with r>255/7 and -1<x≤-84/85 located. Published horizontal restrictions do not establish this angular residual rectangle. The zero-location/product mechanism behind the reduction remains classical.
entries.title: Slope positivity on the remaining rectangular angular region

entries.basis: No exact region x≤-1+(84/167)/r with r>255/7 located. This specific numerical geometry is distinct from the domains of the cited horizontal criteria.
entries.title: Slope positivity on the smaller curved residual region

entries.basis: Every off-line zero lies in a wedge with slope m>|Imρ|/|Reρ−1/2|; all slopes exhaust the off-line strip.
entries.qualification: Classical reformulation identified by explicit mathematical reduction; the exact project wording/name was not located as a separately published criterion. This is not evidence of novelty.
entries.title: Zero exclusion in every positive-slope wedge

entries.basis: An unbounded set of slopes already supplies a wedge containing each fixed off-line zero.
entries.qualification: Classical reformulation identified by explicit mathematical reduction; the exact project wording/name was not located as a separately published criterion. This is not evidence of novelty.
entries.title: Zero exclusion for a cofinal collection of slopes

entries.basis: As m ranges over positive reals, cutoffs (1-m²)/(1+m²) exhaust (-1,1). The all-cutoff condition is an elementary reparametrization of angular derivative positivity; no exact published formulation located.
entries.title: Angular positivity certificates for every slope cutoff

entries.relationship: Centered positive zero-displacement defect built from classical reciprocal-zero identities
entries.basis: No exact published criterion using this rational kernel was located. Each summand is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when delta=0, so the vanishing mechanism is elementary. Gun–Murty–Rath give a related reciprocal-modulus-sum RH criterion with different weights and center.
entries.title: Vanishing actual RR defect

entries.basis: No exact all-height bound C≤3c1/(4T²) located. C is the fixed full defect, not a truncated tail; finiteness of c1 and T→infinity force C=0. This standard limiting argument should not be presented as an independently new asymptotic principle.
entries.title: All-height inverse-square upper bound on the full actual defect

entries.relationship: Exact iff not located; forward central-curvature identity is classical
entries.basis: Known centered secondary-zeta identities use alpha=-i(rho-1/2)=gamma-i delta. Under RH the sum of gamma^-2 over positive-height occurrences equals xi″(1/2)/(2xi(1/2)). The exact converse comparing real-ordinate mass to curvature was not located. Their difference is the elementary positive kernel in E23. Preserve the declaration’s ZetaBinding and TraceIdentification hypotheses.
entries.title: Inverse-height mass equals actual central xi curvature

entries.relationship: E25 plus the constant-defect decay reformulation of E24
entries.basis: No exact primary match located. The additional all-height bound on c1-centerCurvature forces that fixed defect to vanish by a standard limit; preserve both ZetaBinding and TraceIdentification.
entries.title: All-height decay of the central curvature defect

entries.relationship: Bespoke angular integral and critical-line cutoff asymptotic
entries.basis: No exact small-radius little-o remainder with this integral and multiplicity-bearing cutoff located. Classical integral RH criteria exist, but the Balazard–Saias–Yor integral and its truncation rate use log|zeta| on the critical line and are not this angular integral. Standard asymptotics and zero-sum identities should not be called novel.
entries.title: Angular integral remainder is little-o of radius

entries.relationship: Weighted differential continuation applied to the project residual domain
entries.basis: No exact radius-dependent (1+x)A′≤MA criterion with the infimum kappa(r) located. Nonvanishing by integrating a relative derivative bound is standard differential-inequality reasoning; the RH profile/domain specialization is the unlocated part.
entries.title: Finite radius-dependent relative derivative bound on the residual interval

entries.basis: No exact angular F criterion located. Positivity preservation from F′≥-rate F with locally integrable nonnegative rate is the classical integrating-factor/Gronwall mechanism. The application to this theta profile is the potentially new formulation.
entries.title: Locally integrable finite-rate control along the angle

entries.relationship: Elementary local difference-quotient reformulation of E13
entries.basis: For a differentiable profile the quantified increment bound is exactly nonnegative derivative. No exact published RH statement located; the epsilon-eta calculus reformulation is standard and should not count as independent substantive novelty.
entries.title: Arbitrarily small negative linear error in local forward increments

entries.qualification: Classical reformulation identified by explicit mathematical reduction; the exact project wording/name was not located as a separately published criterion. This is not evidence of novelty.

entries.qualification: Classical reformulation identified by explicit mathematical reduction; the exact project wording/name was not located as a separately published criterion. This is not evidence of novelty.

entries.title: Pointwise GP/BKQR one-sided passivity

entries.relationship: Project-specific KQ-tail reformulation; no exact primary-literature match located.
entries.basis: The fixed canonical defect is bounded by every vanishing squared KQ tail. The source uses a chosen algebraic transverse jet and unit binding scales. This is a native-target equivalence in source, but not an identified historical analytic-jet theorem; the potentially novel label applies only to this formulation, without a priority claim.
entries.title: Canonical exact-to-KQ-tail upper bounds

entries.relationship: Project-specific explicit terminal-cell version of the same tail-bound mechanism.
entries.basis: The displayed trigonometric terminal-Phi cell and one-sided dyadic defect were not matched to a primary published RH criterion. It is closely related to E36 and should not be advertised as an independent mechanism merely because the formula is expanded.
entries.title: Raw terminal-Phi cell bound / actual KQ limit core

entries.relationship: Project-specific existential certificate packaging of one-sided passivity.
entries.basis: No exact published counterpart was located. F,T,r are existentially free; no nonnegative energies, specified approximation scheme or convergence of r is required. The reverse takes F=E,T=r=0 under RH. Novelty, if any, is packaging; the existence predicate is not a constructed finite witness.
entries.title: Existence of a one-sided finite-energy factorization

entries.relationship: Project-specific telescoping certificate form of E38.
entries.basis: No exact primary-literature match was located. The finite defect is a telescoping negative-square sum with freely existential cells; the tail is bounded by an arbitrarily small remainder. Treat as a structured variant of E38, not an independent analytical construction or proof that a source exists.
entries.title: Existence of a telescoping negative-square source

entries.basis: The exact theorem has model parameters and NormalizedDyadicMultiplierFacts, Scale2Facts and Background assumptions. No primary published match was located for this Constructor package. The native zero predicate is genuine, but the required calibration, positive energies and tail-smallness facts are hypotheses, not established by the constructor equivalence.
entries.title: Existential two-sided constructor under calibrated background

entries.relationship: Project-specific cofinal-depth specialization of established Widder/Stieltjes theory.
entries.basis: Classical Widder positivity and Stieltjes representation supply background, but no exact published match was established for the frozen rawXi tower and cofinal US. Its iff explicitly assumes downward positivity, Stieltjes slit exclusion and RH-to-all-depth positivity. The raw completion at s=0,1 is not the repaired entire xi used by newer active sources. Do not call the underlying Widder hierarchy new.
entries.title: Cofinal uniform positivity of the frozen raw-xi Widder tower

entries.relationship: Identifiable Zhang/Hausdorff criterion family; exact formal match unverified.
entries.basis: Zhang’s Corollary 6 gives actual Xi-derived real moments and finite-difference RH conditions. Here the coefficient sequence has integer type and opaque origins, and RH is an opaque Prop; ZHANG2023_FRONTIER_ANCHOR supplies the iff as an axiom. Literature attribution is provenance, not verification of this normalization or native RH.
entries.title: Zhang-normalized Hausdorff finite-difference positivity

entries.relationship: Identifiable Zhang complete-monotonicity hierarchy; comment-level match only.
entries.basis: Zhang’s Corollary 4 matches the stated intended hierarchy. The local criterion itself is opaque, with no encoded G_k^(m) or complete-monotonicity definition, and the iff comes from ZHANG2022_FRONTIER_ANCHOR. Classify as literature-inspired model provenance, not a new theorem or verified native match.
entries.title: Zhang complete-monotonicity hierarchy

entries.relationship: Classical Wall–Sokal Hausdorff continued-fraction mechanism; opaque application.
entries.basis: Sokal gives the explicit g_i∈[0,1] continued-fraction characterization. Local WallAdmissible is opaque and the Hausdorff-to-Wall bridge is axiomatized, in addition to the Zhang RH anchor. The canonical coefficients and exact admissibility definition are not verified against the paper.
entries.title: Wall continued-fraction admissibility

entries.relationship: Classical Berger/Gellar–Wallen moment/subnormality mechanism; exact shift unspecified.
entries.basis: A properly normalized contractive weighted shift has a Hausdorff moment description. The project supplies no concrete shift or subnormality definition, and assumes its Hausdorff bridge as an axiom. Weight positivity, normalization and support/boundedness must be matched before asserting exact literature correspondence.
entries.title: Subnormality of the canonical weighted shift

entries.relationship: Classical Agler complete-hypercontractivity mechanism; convention and model match unresolved.
entries.basis: The local bridge is an axiom between opaque propositions. Agler’s `T*^k T^k` convention concerns subnormal contractions of the same T; formulations using `T^k T*^k` concern the adjoint. Since the project defines neither, an exact operator-orientation claim is unsupported. Mark as literature-inspired provenance, not validated equivalence and not a definitive adjoint error.
entries.title: Complete hypercontractivity of the canonical shift

entries.relationship: Bespoke integer Pascal-splitting presentation of classical Hausdorff positivity.
entries.basis: No exact published PascalHopfAnchor criterion was located. The lattice recurrence is the elementary signed-difference identity, so novelty is at most formal presentation. Hopf does not mean a topological Hopf fibration or Hilbert realization here. The RH link still rests on opaque coefficients/RH and the Zhang axiom.
entries.title: Positive Pascal-Hopf realization

entries.relationship: Bespoke natural-number encoding of the M06 lattice.
entries.basis: No exact published BKQREnergyAnchor was located. Taking nonnegative integer cells as Nat energy recodes the signed-difference condition; Gram/contraction aliases add no inner-product or operator laws. Treat this as a possible new implementation/package name, not a new Hausdorff criterion or native RH equivalence.
entries.title: Natural-valued BKQR energy lattice

entries.relationship: Bespoke eventual-exact finite-window presentation; no genuine trace/resolvent object.
entries.basis: No exact published named criterion was located. The reverse uses a constant stage sequence; finiteJet is eventual exact equality on each finite coefficient window. There are no actual resolvents, finite-rank matrices or analytic convergence in the proposition. The opaque Zhang anchor remains its RH input.
entries.title: Positive-stage finite-jet approximation

entries.relationship: Bespoke commuting energy-source presentation of the Pascal lattice.
entries.basis: No exact published MinimalConstructionAnchor was located. The reverse chooses Q=Nat×Nat, and normSq is an arbitrary Nat-valued energy lacking norm laws. Its positive binary splitting is an algebraic packaging of finite-difference positivity; it is not an identified GP Hilbert/operator construction. The RH link is an axiom.
entries.title: Commuting two-branch energy source

entries.relationship: Project-specific abstract-RH package with a classical finite positive-moment ingredient
entries.basis: Tchakaloff identifies the finite positive quadrature ingredient, not the complete named RH package. The exact package has unresolved priority; the classical realization theorem itself is not new. Here hRealize remains an explicit premise, the sequence and RH remain opaque, and the Zhang bridge is axiomatized.
entries.title: Finite positive-kernel approximation of the abstract Xi coefficient sequence

supplementary_entries.title: Native zero rigidity

supplementary_entries.basis: Disk coordinates and nonvanishing factors re-express right-half-plane zero exclusion. This identifies the classical mechanism, not an exact published theorem using this J.

supplementary_entries.title: Scalar and positive-metric passivity
supplementary_entries.basis: The gain 1+4(Re(s)−1/2)²≤1 is elementary zero rigidity; the admitted metric variants encode it. No actual GP/Mellin operator identification follows.

supplementary_entries.title: One fixed seed and all depths
supplementary_entries.basis: The scalar proxy criterion is classical zero rigidity with a seed test and ordinary induction. The globally admitted metric remains the substantive input.

supplementary_entries.title: Finite metric code plus global calibration
supplementary_entries.basis: Exact checker/calibration packaging has unresolved priority. Rational positivity alone does not check NativeCalibrated, and the genuine checker iff retains soundness and completeness premises.

supplementary_entries.title: Actual Hardy disk exhaustion
supplementary_entries.basis: Exact J/energy/defect packaging has unresolved priority. ActualHardyEnergy and positivity on whole compact disks remain hypotheses; the finite integer is not a finite Boolean test.

supplementary_entries.title: Prescribed-radius successor
supplementary_entries.basis: A project-specific reformulation of the preceding conditional disk criterion. Ordinary induction is classical; the radius-enlargement premise is still required.

supplementary_entries.title: Actual Widder control versus off-line explosion
supplementary_entries.basis: Project-specific conditional sufficient criterion using classical moment-transform ideas. All-order calibration and off-line explosion remain explicit inputs; this is not a proved iff.

supplementary_entries.title: Cofinal actual moments, central cells and finite trace limits
supplementary_entries.basis: Exact KQ/SOLOBOLO realization and source interfaces have unresolved priority. Channel analysis and finite-trace convergence remain required inputs to one-way implications.

supplementary_entries.title: Finite-rate semantic admissions
supplementary_entries.basis: Exact rational-packet packaging has unresolved priority. An all-index semantic bound and a custom RH/source interface remain; no native Mathlib RH equivalence is supplied here.

supplementary_entries.title: Centered zero geometry and subexponential moments
supplementary_entries.basis: Project-specific conditional moment/pole packaging; the growth-versus-pole argument is standard. Actual-zero coverage and analytic hypotheses are retained, and these are sufficient implications.

master_chain.basis: Exact project packaging has unresolved priority. Scalar, integral and Hilbert-space mechanisms are standard; MASTER_1, MASTER_2 and integrability remain explicit hypotheses.
